lc_person: James B. Wood (born 1946), Williams College historian; author of The Nobility of the Election of Bayeux, 1463-1666 and The King's Army.
item_person: James Wood, historian and university teacher, identified by the same LC, BnF and GND authorities; Wikidata states birth year 1943.

evidence.says: LC heading is Wood, James B., 1946-. Its source is The Nobility of the Election of Bayeux (1980); the publisher information places him in the Williams College History Department, and the CIP data sheet supplies birth year 1946.

James Wood is classified as a historian and university teacher. Identifiers include LC n79113385, BnF 123746915, GND 172508770 and VIAF 112928744. The 1943 birth claim cites Persée authority 238873; the BNB identifier itself contains WoodJamesB1946-.

BnF identifies James B. Wood as born in 1946 and a Williams College history professor, citing the 1980 Bayeux book and Japanese Military Strategy in the Pacific War (2007). This is the BnF authority linked by Wikidata.

The German National Library identifies James B. Wood, variant James Brian Wood, as a historian and university teacher at Williams College, with birth year 1946. This is the GND authority linked by Wikidata.
The graph's Open Library author is Wood, James B., with birth year 1946.
This author's works are The King's Army and The Nobility of the Election of Bayeux, 1463-1666, matching the LC author and the subject of the graph's dissertation.

Williams College identifies James Wood as its history professor and author of Japanese Military Strategy in the Pacific War, and states that he earned his Ph.D. at Emory University in 1973, matching the graph's dissertation institution and year.

The authority cited for Wikidata's birth claim identifies Wood, James, also James B. Wood, as a Williams College historian and links the Bayeux and King's Army books. The retrieved page displays no birth year.

notes: The matching works, affiliation, doctoral institution/year and authority identifiers establish the identity despite the birth discrepancy. LC, BnF and DNB support 1946; Wikidata's 1943 claim is not supported by the currently displayed Persée page. No replacement QID is needed.
